Comments (English): [ 3 new kitchen appliances in 12 months ] || ---------------- || First, our old Refrig broke. That took 5 months: backordered; loaner; lemon that the brand said was "normal;" refund; switched brand and retailer before we were finally satisfied. It wasn't the retailer's fault. After a weekend of handwishing I took the model number of our old dishwasher to my weekly breakfast with the guys. I was going to drive to a local store I like to end my handwashing, inefficient misery. After breakfast I was walking to my car (PHEV) when I noticed an appliance store I've driven past a thousand times, and never seen. I went in and met the guys. Said that I needed Bosch. I was shown and given details about 3 Bosch possibilities. My wife met me there later that day. She had already selected one of the 3. I signed the paperwork. Easy install too if I can do it, which I did to save a few bucks. Looks great. Did a swell job on the install. The new Bosch is totally quiet (quieter than the old one, which was quiet) and efficient. I'm a sustainability nut. Cool options. Love the "Rinse" button and adjustable top (3rd) shelf. Button push, middle shelf tilt feature for bigger stuff on one side of bottom, is cool. Say pasta cooker lid. Did I say Quiet? Red light on the floor when working. Haven't used the "pop open" feature yet. Did I say Quiet? What does a dishwasher do? It washes the dishes really well. Oh, and now I can hang my towel on the handle, not across the kitchen on the once shared stove handle. Before now, never had a kitchen handle of my own. The third and final kitchen appliance, an induction range story, is for another time.

Sentence (English): (This review was received through a promotion.)
Comments (English): [ Lots of flexibility in space and little noise ] || ---------------- || (This review was received through a promotion.) Very good flexibility in arranging the interior space which means fewer uses of the dishwasher. It also allows you to better separate cutlery, glasses, pans and saucepans. Now I can put the dishwasher on at any time and when the door is automatically opened the cutlery does not rust and dries better. Very good flexibility to program the ignition. I will use the cleaning program sometime because I think the current one failed for that reason. Little noisy. The steel tank with a 10-year guarantee. What I like least is the feeling that the trays do not adjust in height, nor do they move very smoothly, but not much. In general very good for the moment.
Comments (Original): [ Mucha flexibilidad en el espacio y poco ruido ] || ---------------- || (Esta reseña se ha recibido a través de una promoción.) El programa de limpieza lo usaré alguna vez porque el actual creo que falló por ese motivo. Poco ruidoso. La cuba de acero con garantía de 10 años.Lo que menos me gusta es la sensación de que las bandejas no se ajustan en altura, ni se desplazan muy suaves, pero poca cosa.En general muy bien por el momento.

A sparse and not very functional interior design. The cutlery basket does not fit with anything, so it is loose and unstable. You have no possibility to lower only one side of the upper basket. The upper fastening of the furniture panel is flimsy and is just in the part that suffers the most traction. The screws are shallow and the panel is held very little and poorly, so it ends up coming off. The panel, being sliding, takes up a lot of space when lowering the door. The folding rods of the lower basket do not give much play as they are the same as the fixed ones. Sentence (English): I had my old KitchenAid DW for 21 years!
Comments (English): [ Getting used to it ] || ---------------- || I had my old KitchenAid DW for 21 years! I loved it, and because of its durability, I wanted another KitchenAid. I like this one too, but change takes some getting used to. The tines on the lower and middle racks are a little further apart than my old one and I am learning how to load the dishes again. I can't place a jar lid on either of those racks because it may fall through. The DW also has the 3rd rack at the top for flatware. I still use the flatware basket, but I put things like serving spoons and spatulas and those pesky jar lids on the 3rd rack. None of the tines fold down to accommodate odd or larger shaped items. The quality of the wash and dry on the Normal cycle is excellent. The cycle takes longer than in my old DW. My old DW had a timer display on the front so I could tell how many minutes I had left to wait. I don't have that display on the new DW. It is incredibly quiet! I've used the Express wash with dry heat. It does a good job cleaning too, but the dishes are not as dry at the end of the cycle. Over all, I believe I'm going to be happy with the new DW once this old dog learns all the new tricks :)

Sentence (English): The saying "buying time with money" really holds true.
Comments (English): [ I regret buying it now ] || ---------------- || The saying "buying time with money" really holds true. I worried whether it would wash better than hand-washing, and I kept putting it in my cart and agonizing over it. Then, the price suddenly seemed reasonable (around 690,000 won with a credit card discount), so I bought it. My worries up until then were for nothing. It's cleaner than the ones I've done myself. Living alone, I don't think I have much to wash, but if I put it off all weekend because it's a hassle, by Sunday evening, I'd be overwhelmed with the amount of dishes I'd have to do. But now, it's so much easier. To cut down on the dishes, I used to reuse my water cup and eat side dishes straight from the container. Now, it's amazing how I use a fresh cup every time I drink water and put my side dishes in a bowl. I didn't think I'd need steam or hot air drying, so I debated between the cost-effective DUBJ1EP and the DUBJ1E, which I bought. They have the same features, but the difference was whether it had two or three shelves and whether it had Wi-Fi. I'm glad I chose the three-shelf model. I liked putting utensils like spoons, knives, and ladles on the top shelf. The two-shelf model seems to have a separate spoon holder at the bottom, but I'm not good at Tetris, so I didn't have enough space at the bottom. If I had chosen the two-shelf model, the spoon holder would have taken up space at the bottom, making it inconvenient to use. If you're looking for a model that sticks to basic functions without needing steam or hot air drying like I do, I recommend the DUBJ1E! Oh, and the delivery was really fast, and I was able to do it on my own, which was nice. I live alone, so I only have time on weekends, but I made a reservation for Saturday. The sink installer came at 9:00 AM to do the installation, and the dishwasher installer came at 11:00 AM to do the installation. The installers were very friendly and did a great job of cleaning up the area. I wanted to install 600 units, so they installed 800 units. They had to put in a door in the remaining space, which cost me 200,000 won. But seeing the installer do the installation made me think it was a good deal. Considering various aspects, I carefully compared two models of a 500,000 won dishwasher and a 1 million won bespoke model, and purchased a supply-type dishwasher. <Ascon issue> . I was hesitant to buy a Samsung dishwasher because there was a review saying that Samsung used ascon as a noise shielding material, so it smelled a lot. This model is also promoted as a butyl even though it is a product released in 20 years in Chinese factory production. In fact, it smells a bit when I first started it up, but it's not to the point where I can't stand it like I said in the reviews, so I think it's okay. <Dry function> . Products over 500,000 won do not have a drying function. There is a function called drying, but the residual heat of hot water removes the water in the bowl, so the performance of products in the 1 million won range is incomparable. However, the 60A5055 product also has an automatic door open function 2 minutes before the end, so all the water in the bowl is dry when you come back after going out. Even when there was no dishwasher, I didn't wash the dishes and kept them, and since I dried them naturally on a drying rack, it seems that the water drying from the hot dishes is enough for me. And this product also has a slight drying function, but if you add rinse aid and so on, it takes 1 hour and 55 minutes. I didn't use the drying function and used 55 minutes + natural drying, but I liked the short washing time. <Washability> . Delivery came this morning and I turned the dishwasher twice. Yesterday, while ordering the dishwasher, I ordered the detergent online, but the dishwasher arrived faster than the detergent, so there was no dedicated detergent. Inevitably, I applied only dish detergent that produced little bubbles and operated it as if I was rinsing it in the dishwasher. When purchasing this product, the most worrying feature was that there are three upper, middle and lower parts where water comes out, and there is no jet (?) water nozzle in the 1 million won range, so it will not be washable. After using it twice, I think it's fine. I'll try to measure the pH again tomorrow. I was wondering if there would be any residual detergent. <Operating Touch Bar> . This is the model with the operating touch bar on the front. These days, it's hidden on the top, so you have to open the door to operate it, but it's on the front because it was designed three years ago. After I start cleaning, no matter how many times I press the button, it doesn't work. It's okay for babies to press it at home, and it's nice to be able to see how many minutes are left. Overall, I am satisfied with the purchase as a model with good value for money. After lunch, I left all the dishes and came out, but I didn't get my clothes wet from splashing water while washing the dishes, and I had a lot of time to prepare for going out, so I could understand why they said aunt when looking at the dishwasher. If you are thinking about it, hurry up and buy it! I would like to include one of my in-laws and relatives. I don't think I'll ever have wrist pain.

Sentence (English): Excellent dish washer.
Comments (English): [ Excellent product. Poor installation experience. ] || ---------------- || Excellent dish washer. Definitely do not use Costco for delivery & installation. I should have picked this up myself and watched YouTube for installation instructions, initially. Yet, I decided to try Costco, because why not, right? I patiently waited the 2 weeks for delivery & installation, and paid extra for all the required new change parts, yet upon delivery, the delivery/installation technicians said they're unable to install my new dishwasher because they didn't bring the right size connection hose, and just left the big box in my kitchen, with the top off and making sure they took a photo to confirm delivery. I know it was a late delivery and very cold outside, so I understand wanting to go home to your family, but I'm just writing this to help the next person. My desperate self even offered $50 cash if they just use the existing hose that I have, with a hard "no" response. I was sad for a moment, then watched a YouTube video and did the unboxing and installation myself, with my existing hose. Honestly, the unboxing was harder then the actual installation, because the dishwasher was screwed down to a wooden mini-pallet and the screws were difficult to remove from underneath. Hope this helps someone. Have a wonderful day. -Danny

I patiently waited the 2 weeks for delivery & installation, and paid extra for all the required new change parts, yet upon delivery, the delivery/installation technicians said they're unable to install my new dishwasher because they didn't bring the right size connection hose, and just left the big box in my kitchen, with the top off and making sure they took a photo to confirm delivery. I know it was a late delivery and very cold outside, so I understand wanting to go home to your family, but I'm just writing this to help the next person. My desperate self even offered $50 cash if they just use the existing hose that I have, with a hard 'no' response. I was sad for a moment, then watched a YouTube video and did the unboxing and installation myself, with my existing hose. Honestly, the unboxing was harder then the actual installation, because the dishwasher was screwed down to a wooden mini-pallet and the screws were difficult to remove from underneath. Hope this helps someone. Have a wonderful day. -Danny

Sentence (English): I bought this dishwasher six months ago and have regretted it every since.
Comments (English): [ Expensive, takes forever to wash, dishes don't fit ] || ---------------- || I bought this dishwasher six months ago and have regretted it every since. The normal cycle takes over two hours, and unless you are hyper-vigilant about topping up the rinse-aid, your dishes will be wet at the end. The bottom rack has one adjustable set of tines and that's it. The tines are so close together (even after adjusting) that this rack only fits a few dishes at a time. Use a lot of small bowls? Forget washing more than a few at a time, since they don't sit in the rack properly. In addition to the maddening design of the racks and eternity this machine takes to wash, the top control panel has two cracks in it already and needs to be replaced. The one positive of this machine is that it is incredibly quiet. Avoid if you value your sanity and want to wash a full load of dishes at a time.

Sentence (English): I had a great dishwasher before, but I didn't know my glassware, silverware, and pots could achieve this level of shine.
Comments (English): [ Quiet, sparkling, good dry ] || ---------------- || I had a great dishwasher before, but I didn't know my glassware, silverware, and pots could achieve this level of shine. The new dishwasher does a great job of getting them sparkling clean. It's quiet and efficient. It does a good job of getting them dry with ProDry, just a little water in the tops of cups. I always clean off debris first but it has done fine with smeared bowls. The third rack on top holds shorter glasses on the left, and the right side is nice for knives. With the addition of the third rack, I am able to cram a lot more stuff in so I'm not running the dishwasher as frequently, which is nice. The basket covers for the utensils are removable. Our silverware is a little large for some of the slots, so I removed one of the covers, but it's a nice feature because it does space the silverware out well so that it gets cleaner. One thing to note is that the wash/dry cycle for ProWash or Normal takes almost 3 hours. You can use the express wash for a faster wash, but I believe it uses more water and energy so you won't get the eco-friendly savings. ProDry can sometimes be shorter because it assesses the level of soil on the dishes. I do want to note that our order from Kitchenaid took over a month to arrive, but they did schedule our delivery time two weeks in advance. We are happy with the experience.

Sentence (English): Costco is no longer handling delivery and installation, regardless of what you may think.
Comments (English): [ Worst experience. ] || ---------------- || Costco is no longer handling delivery and installation, regardless of what you may think. Instead, you have to deal with third parties that are unreliable, rude and flat out liars. Costco can give, as nice as their representatives are, no assistance in the process. I had a driver show up to deliver and install this item, only to tell me he couldn't because my water valve was broken (no visual indication of this, apparently just his hunch) and I would need to get it replaced and reschedule. I had a licensed plumber come out (he arrived 30 minutes after the delivery driver left). He inspected the valve in question, operated it several times, and said it was perfectly functional and up to code. When I contacted the third party again and told them I had paid a plumber to tell me my valve was fine (and you know plumbers are more than happy to take money from you for a job if it's needed) and they need to send the driver back out to install the dishwasher he left in my living room they told me they could come out again next week! I said no, this was your mistake, come make it right! If not today, tomorrow. They put me on hold and came back a few minutes later asking me what kind of piping I have? I asked why that was relevant, and they said the driver said the piping wasn't to code (again, a licensed plumber just said it was). I asked if their driver was a licensed plumber, to which they replied no, but he is an experienced installer. Well, a licensed plumber beats a delivery driver and installer when it comes to determining whether or not something is up to code, correct? ( My home is 15 years old for Pete's sake). They argued with me in that point, and said it was their policy and was in writing. When the call ended, I downloaded GE's policy from their site, and that was not a requirement. Spoke to Costco reps, who explained they had no control of the situation and attempted to contact the GE reps and their local affiliate to no avail. I reached another GE department, explained the situation, quoted them their own guidelines from the website and they eventually said the other reps were wrong, and they would install it. However their local affiliate wouldn't come back out for a week! Meanwhile I have no dishwasher! I called Costco back, told them this was unacceptable and I needed them to give me a refund so I can go to another local seller and get one installed by tomorrow. They said no problem on the refund, but they would need to pickup the item first. Again the explained it's a third party delivery service, and contacting them it would take a week for pickup! This whole process took 5 hours of phone time, a $150 charge from a plumber to tell me everything is good on my end, and I still wasn't going to have a dishwasher for a week. I eventually got Costco to issue me a partial credit to hire a plumber (the same one I had called earlier) to install it. I had it installed the next morning, and ended up, even with the credit, $200 more out of pocket total.This experience is not isolated to this item. Since Costco began contracting their delivery and installation services a couple of years ago this is the third horrible experience. We will not be purchasing big ticket items via their website any longer.As to the dishwasher, it performs well so far, with the exception of not being nearly as quite as advertised.

We're a week and a half into ownership and have run both large and small loads through it, and it's handled everything with ease. The feature I think deserves a lot more attention is CrystalDry, which is an incredibly clever and elegantly designed drying system that effectively dries everything, including plastics, while not requiring the use of a heating element. Just spend the extra money, you won't regret it.

Sentence (English): Absolutely love this dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ KitchenAid Hits A Home Run! ] || ---------------- || Absolutely love this dishwasher. Significantly more room (better layout) than the Bosch it replaced and the flexibility inside is even better than my 20 year old KitchenAid I left when we moved. I read a lot of reviews before going to see one in person. The long wash/dry cycle is because of our DOE friends as all of the current dishwashers are like that. I have always prerinsed dishes before loading in a dishwasher and so I typically run the express wash cycle along with the prodry (you have wash options and dry options to choose from - make sure you chose a dry cycle or you will have wet dishes! ). I learned long ago to leave the door shut for about an hour leaving the residual heat to finish drying dishes and continue to do that with this dishwasher. Removing the bottom level first keeps any water from rimmed coffee mugs from falling on dry dishes. The options for washing and drying in this dishwasher give great flexibility and since I run my gold rimmed china in the dishwasher, that is important to me! There are four stemware holders to keep wine glasses safe that are easy to use. We have stemless glasses which fit beautifully on the very top rack along with little things like small bowls, measuring cups, coffee mugs, etc. This frees up the other two racks so that I can fit everything in and room for more. The Bosch filled up in a couple of days with plenty of dishes left to either hand wash or wait for the next load. Not so with this KitchenAid. We have had this installed for two weeks and hope it lasts at least as long as our last one. BTW, the ProWash and ProDry cycle combo does take awhile, but the dishes came out clean and dry. Very quiet with just enough volume in the kitchen to know that it is going. It has logical placements for kitchenware. I removed one of the silverware covers [slides off], filling one side as designed and the other for oversize silverware/serving utensils. It is easy to accidentally hit the wash/dry buttons, but that was true of the old Bosch that had buttons in front. Don't worry about that for if you don't shut the door within four seconds, everything cancels anyway - or push the cancel button and be done with it. Racks glide SO smoothly and it is thrifty in how much soap and rinse aid it takes. The front right that changes colors as it goes through cycles, so you can see across the room at a glance what it is doing. It is gorgeous and I love the handlebar for dishtowels. The only thing that would make it better is going back to the old fast cycle times of old, but I don't think we will see that anytime soon.

Removing the bottom level first keeps any water from rimmed coffee mugs from falling on dry dishes.  The options for washing and drying in this dishwasher give great flexibility and since I run my gold rimmed china in the dishwasher, that is important to me!  There are four stemware holders to keep wine glasses safe that are easy to use.  We have stemless glasses which fit beautifully on the very top rack along with little things like small bowls, measuring cups, coffee mugs, etc. This frees up the other two racks so that I can fit everything in and room for more. We have had this installed for two weeks and hope it lasts at least as long as our last one.  BTW, the ProWash and ProDry cycle combo does take awhile, but the dishes came out clean and dry. Very quiet with just enough volume in the kitchen to know that it is going.  It has logical placements for kitchenware.  I removed one of the silverware covers [slides off], filling one side as designed and the other for oversize silverware/serving utensils.  It is easy to accidentally hit the wash/dry buttons, but that was true of the old Bosch that had buttons in front. Don't worry about that for if you don't shut the door within four seconds, everything cancels anyway - or push the cancel button and be done with it.  Racks glide SO smoothly and it is thrifty in how much soap and rinse aid it takes.  The front right that changes colors as it goes through cycles, so you can see across the room at a glance what it is doing.  It is gorgeous and I love the handlebar for dishtowels.  The only thing that would make it better is going back to the old fast cycle times of old, but I don't think we will see that anytime soon.

Sentence (English): [House App - *******].
Comments (English): [House App - *******]. While I was fighting an illness, my mother helped me with housework for almost a year at my house. There was a time when I was temporarily free from the privilege of washing dishes as a patient. Thanks to my mother, I was able to live comfortably during my fight against the illness, but I thought it would never come to me. As my fight against the illness came to an end, my mother returned to her original home. However, I started to do housework myself again like before I was a patient. After the surgery, my arm discomfort never recovered, so it became very difficult for me to wash the dishes every time. With the pain in my arm that continued all day long. Since then, I gradually remembered the days when I was free from the dishes my mother used to do. I wanted to buy a dishwasher to replace it. I chose the DUB22WA model that was just right for my white sink ^^. Stainless steel washing blades, 100-degree True Steam that is completely free from bacteria. High-temperature drying, high-temperature sterilization, etc. It was exactly what I wanted ^^. LG Dios dishwasher that washes dishes better than me! I have children, so there are a lot of dishes every time I wash dishes, but it is so good that I can adjust the smart shelf to the amount of dishes for a household of 4. Every time I see the door quietly opening after quietly washing late at night, I feel satisfied and grateful for the free time I have. I run the dishwasher every time I do three meals. Adding the safe rinse to the standard course completely reduced the strain on my arms for about 2 hours and 6 minutes. I am so glad that I bought the LG Dios dishwasher that makes me feel comfortable, like my mother washes the dishes. My arms, which became uncomfortable after surgery, are so precious that I have to take care of them for the rest of my life! I love you! LG! Thank you for researching and making such a great dishwasher. It is the best gift for me.

Sentence (English): Organization of pegs is terrible.
Comments (English): [ Lots of issues - sometimes it works ] || ---------------- || Organization of pegs is terrible. You either can't fit your dishes in the right side because they're too thick, or you have to space them every other slot if you want them to anywhere near clean. There are tons of issues with interior design with this model that I don't have time to describe right now.The first 3 days it cleaned fine. After that it will only clean at all (with 1-4 not clean dishes per load) if I load it up with pure citric acid (2 tbsp + detergent pod), run my hot water through my sink AND set the dishwasher to 'heavy wash.' Otherwise it's dirty, smelly dishes that are not clean. The corners of the racks don't get clean at all. Why have that space there if the dishwasher won't clean in those areas? Why not make the tray smaller? The handle on the top rack holds water so when the dishes are done and you pull it out, it gets all of the dishes below wet with soiled water that has been standing for a while. I honestly don't know how this product made it through quality control. Luckily this was given to me as a gift, so it's not a real loss for me. I do see myself having to replace this much sooner than I would've otherwise. I would not recommend this dishwasher to anyone spending their own money on it. Issues all around.

Sentence (English): This dishwasher was replacing an 8-year old Kenmore Elite that had several repairs in the previous year.
Comments (English): [ Cleans and Dries Beautifully ] || ---------------- || This dishwasher was replacing an 8-year old Kenmore Elite that had several repairs in the previous year. We had two requirements: it must be quiet (open floor plan with a TV nearby) and handle-less (dishwasher is built into a corner with drawers next to it.). This dishwasher is 39 dB. The only sound we hear is the water swishing as it cleans--very, very quiet. I think 42 dB would have been quiet enough for our needs, and anything 44dB or less is considered \"quiet.\". This dishwasher cleans well enough that I only have to use the 60 minute wash for everything. Such an improvement since we used to need a 2:50 wash to get anything clean before. Also, the door that opens automatically at the end of the cycle is wonderful! The dishes are completely dry if left for a couple hours or overnight. It works even better than a heated dry cycle. I love it. I wasn't sure I would like three racks, but even with the third top rack, there is enough room for plates and tall cups on the other two racks. The plates on the bottom rack in the image are Corelle dinner plates and our 10 3/4\" Mikasa plates also fit. The cup on the top rack in the image is a 14-oz tumbler. My 20-oz Contigo travel mug also fits in the top rack. The shallow third rack is the only place that my snapware lids fit very well, and they do collect a little bit of water since they are flat, however this is a small price to pay when absolutely everything else dries completely. The third rack is also awesome for plastic chopsticks and other small items that used to fall through the racks in my other dishwasher. The only downside to this dishwasher is that we use a lot of bowls, and the bottom rack configuration is not good for very many cereal-sized bowls. It is designed for plates with an open area (no tines) for mixing bowls or pots. To compensate, we put most bowls on the top rack and move some mugs to the bottom rack area where there are no tines. Overall, this dishwasher is amazingly quiet, washes well and quickly, dries beautifully, and has hidden buttons to avoid accidentally canceling a cycle if I lean against it (which used to happen all the time with our other dishwasher.) The surface is easy to clean, doesn't seem to show fingerprints or smudges very much, and (bonus! ) doesn't even have a raised brand logo on the front, making it even easier to wipe down and keep clean. I am delighted with this purchase, and hoping that it stays repair-free for many years!

Comments (English): [ Good Appliance Terrible Customer Service ] || ---------------- || The dishwasher works fine, although we only had it for a couple of days so time will tell. The biggest issue is that there was no indication (as in clear warning) that the appliance was not delivered with a standard power cord, which is quite surprising at this price point. Yes, you have the option to pick the additional kit when you checkout but this is not obvious for a nonprofessional first time buyer. I ended up spending a lot of time recycling the spare parts from my old dishwasher. Yes, I could have paid more for professional installation, but I was not expecting it to be such a hassle only because of this. My biggest concern is about the customer service though, with more than a half an hour wait time. I was told that it is what it is when many customers call…. not good, the company should get sufficient staff to answer quicker. I was calling to inquire about the abundant amount of water dripping out whilst unpacking, as well as the very visible existing water stains. I was told this is because of the testing but then one can reasonably expect that the appliances is properly cleaned and dry before delivery. I did not get any excuse. Only offered repetitively to initiate a return if I was not happy and purchase additional parts to make up for what was in my opinion missing. So far no issue with the dishwasher itself. It works fine but I am praying that will not have to ring their customer service again in case anything goes wrong. My level of confidence in the support that the brand can provide is very low.

Sentence (English): This dishwasher was replacing an 8-year old Kenmore Elite that had several repairs in the previous year.
Comments (English): [ Cleans and Dries Beautifully ] || ---------------- || This dishwasher was replacing an 8-year old Kenmore Elite that had several repairs in the previous year. We had two requirements: it must be quiet (open floor plan with a TV nearby) and handle-less (dishwasher is built into a corner with drawers next to it.)This dishwasher is 39 dB. The only sound we hear is the water swishing as it cleans--very, very quiet. I think 42 dB would have been quiet enough for our needs, and anything 44dB or less is considered "quiet."This dishwasher cleans well enough that I only have to use the 60 minute wash for everything. Sentence (English): This was advertised as the quietest dishwasher out there, which is a must have in our open kitchen, and I must say, it's impressive.
Comments (English): [ I LOVE My New Dishwasher! ] || ---------------- || This was advertised as the quietest dishwasher out there, which is a must have in our open kitchen, and I must say, it's impressive. I'll hear the rinse cycle, but the rest of the time it's so quiet I have to see if the red light is shining on the floor (a genius feature, by the way). Probably my favorite feature is the 3rd top rack. For some bizarre reason, my husband insists on loading the flatware in fork and spoons down, which meant many years of bent tines. I couldn't take it anymore and specifically selected this Bosch because it has the 3rd flatware rack. All of the racks took a bit of getting used to. Dishes and glasses sit differently than in our old dishwasher, but the manual does come with helpful diagrams on how to best lay out your flatware (It also comes with a traditional flatware basket for you die-hards. I hid that away so my husband wouldn't use it). The upper rack adjusts up and down to fit tall items, which I haven't yet used, as well as drop down guides for stemware. It also holds way more than our old LG. It does a great job cleaning and I definitely don't miss having to scrape plates before loading. Another feature that really impresses me is the dry cycle. Yes, it's loooong, but I have NEVER had a dishwasher dry EVERYTHING so thoroughly, including plastic ware. I also love that I was able to install it with a custom panel that matched my kitchen cabinets so that it visually disappears when not in use. I still haven't yet tried out all the features and settings, but, all in all, I have zero complaints. I am VERY happy with my new Bosch Benchmark and would definitely buy one again.

I'll hear the rinse cycle, but the rest of the time it's so quiet I have to see if the red light is shining on the floor (a genius feature, by the way). Probably my favorite feature is the 3rd top rack. For some bizarre reason, my husband insists on loading the flatware in fork and spoons down, which meant many years of bent tines. I couldn't take it anymore and specifically selected this Bosch because it has the 3rd flatware rack. All of the racks took a bit of getting used to. Dishes and glasses sit differently than in our old dishwasher, but the manual does come with helpful diagrams on how to best lay out your flatware (It also comes with a traditional flatware basket for you die-hards. It also holds way more than our old LG. It does a great job cleaning and I definitely don't miss having to scrape plates before loading. Another feature that really impresses me is the dry cycle. Yes, it's loooong, but I have NEVER had a dishwasher dry EVERYTHING so thoroughly, including plastic ware. I also love that I was able to install it with a custom panel that matched my kitchen cabinets so that it visually disappears when not in use. I still haven't yet tried out all the features and settings, but, all in all, I have zero complaints. I am VERY happy with my new Bosch Benchmark and would definitely buy one again.

Think twice before buying a GE dishwasher and having Home Depot install it. This is the worst appliance experience I have ever had.

Sentence (English): Bought in April of 2022, directly from Samsung.
Comments (English): [ Buyer's remorse, broken in 9 months of use ] || ---------------- || Bought in April of 2022, directly from Samsung. It is already broken, and awaiting repair, which presently, means we will have been without our dishwasher for 2 weeks. This purchase was a mistake that I wish I could take back. First the ordering experience was terrible. Samsung could not figure out how to sell me an extended service plan as this model was too new. Whatever, I thought, I get an extra year from my CC company. Cleaning power: The dishwasher ONLY cleans if you run it on the most energy-intensive settings. Meaning, Heavy, Sanitize, etc. all selected. You cannot use fast wash, normal etc. unless you just want Luke-warm water and a half-dissolved dishwasher pack thrown at your dirty dishes. It does NOT matter how lightly you load the dishwasher, "Normal", does not clean, and often leaves undissolved packed on the bottom of the dishwasher.Racks: Racks are pretty good. The top-most rack is great for cutlery, knives, spatulas and even small bowls. The middle rack adjust for larger dishes which is really useful for when you want to wash larger items on the bottom rack. The bottom rack is the worst of three racks. It could use some engineering attention, but all in all, it passes as good enough. The tines bend somewhat easily, but that's not a major issue in my eye's. The bottom rack also, according to the manual needs to be loaded a specific way to ensure drying works (will cover later).Drying: Picked this dishwasher because I believe it was be a huge step up in drying over our last. It does NOT matter how lightly you load the dishwasher, 'Normal', does not clean, and often leaves undissolved packed on the bottom of the dishwasher.Racks: Racks are pretty good. The top-most rack is great for cutlery, knives, spatulas and even small bowls. The middle rack adjust for larger dishes which is really useful for when you want to wash larger items on the bottom rack. The bottom rack is the worst of three racks. It could use some engineering attention, but all in all, it passes as good enough. The tines bend somewhat easily, but that's not a major issue in my eye's. The bottom rack also, according to the manual needs to be loaded a specific way to ensure drying works (will cover later).Drying: Picked this dishwasher because I believe it was be a huge step up in drying over our last. The dishwasher opens and makes noise like it wants to dry the dishes, but it's performance is equal the 9-year old unit it replaced that does not open automatically or have fancy marketing around an under-powered fan that does pretty much nothing besides make noise.Connected: SmartThings integration is neat. But it's not something we use regularly. I would not make a purchasing decision based on this for any major appliance. We have Samsung TVs, and Washer/Dryer etc. The limitations of what you can do, and probably for good reason, mean that you can't 'really' be like, 'oh, I forgot to start the washer! Let me pick a cycle and do it while we're driving far away...' nope, can't do it.

Sentence (English): We purchased this unit on 12/05/22 and it was installed on 12/08/22.
Comments (English): [ Bosch SHEM63 ] || ---------------- || We purchased this unit on 12/05/22 and it was installed on 12/08/22. The old unit was 12 yrs old and not a Bosch, but several people had Bosch and were happy with their unit. The controls are simple and the rinse aid indicator is a plus. The unit has several settings but so far we have only usedAuto and Normal. The loading tips in the book have helped but I am still getting used to the difference in the racks to position cups, cutlery, plates, bowls, etc (vs. old unit). The unit is very quiet, and is doing a great job cleaning everything so far. The only minus is some cups have water in the base after the cycle. I am still trying different locations in the 2nd rack to minimize this and watching the rinse aid warning. Overall, we are very pleased with this unit.

Sentence (English): The dishwasher was delivered.
Comments (English): [ Delivered with broken sump ] || ---------------- || The dishwasher was delivered. I installed it and it worked for about a month. The sump is a plastic piece holding wash water and housing the filter, pump, and diverter. The diverter has an optical sensor to tell the computer where water is flowing: to the upper, middle, or lower racks. The nubs where the diverter mounts were broken and it took about a month of vibrating for the optical sensor to be so far out of alignment for an error code to be generated. I called kitchenAid to schedule warranty service. Service was scheduled and I was given the local service providers phone number. A few days later I called to make sure I was scheduled and the local provider had not been sent the information. So I tried again. Long wait on first call, about 50minutes, and about a 20minute wait on second. I'm pretty handy so took the unit apart to find the problem. I found the service manual online and interpreted the error code, identified components, etc. I noticed the diverter mount was broken but more importantly this: SOMEONE HAD TRIED TO GLUE IT BACK ON! This type of soft plastic, given temperature variation (the hot and cold of washing) makes it very difficult for any glue to hold. The glue they attempted to use was very weak for this application. It's almost like wood glue.

The diverter has an optical sensor to tell the computer where water is flowing: to the upper, middle, or lower racks. The nubs where the diverter mounts were broken and it took about a month of vibrating for the optical sensor to be so far out of alignment for an error code to be generated. I called kitchenAid to schedule warranty service. Service was scheduled and I was given the local service providers phone number. A few days later I called to make sure I was scheduled and the local provider had not been sent the information. So I tried again. Long wait on first call, about 50minutes, and about a 20minute wait on second. I'm pretty handy so took the unit apart to find the problem. I found the service manual online and interpreted the error code, identified components, etc. I noticed the diverter mount was broken but more importantly this: SOMEONE HAD TRIED TO GLUE IT BACK ON! This type of soft plastic, given temperature variation (the hot and cold of washing) makes it very difficult for any glue to hold. The glue they attempted to use was very weak for this application. It's almost like wood glue.

Sentence (English): I have only had the dishwasher installed for a week and so far the product itself is okay.
Comments (English): [ Costco Installation Service a Disaster ] || ---------------- || I have only had the dishwasher installed for a week and so far the product itself is okay. However, the installation process was a complete nightmare. I had the dishwasher delivered along with a new refrigerator. The notes on the order said that someone would contact me about installation but I never got a call so I call customer service and made an appointment. Was supposed to get a call the night before with time, but never came so I called the next day only to find out there was a 'problem' with the service request so they make a second appointment for me. Same thing - no one called or showed. I called for a third time and got someone who knew what they were doing. Turns out the first two appointments were not made with the 3rd party installer as required (training issue? ). So finally - 10 days after delivery (during which time the new dishwasher is sitting in middle of my kitchen) - an installer shows up, but can't get the old dishwasher out. Tells me his truck is in the shop and he doesn't have the tools he needs but he'll come back in a couple of days. Get a call from Costco with new appointment, but when the day rolls around it is a different installer. No one has told him about the issues encountered by the first installer, but he comes anyway and is able to get the old dishwasher out and install the new one. When he is done he calls me in the kitchen and the front of the dishwasher is crooked. One side is lined up with the counter and the other sticks out at least an inch. He tells me it is because the space under the counter is crooked and there is nothing he can do. So now I'm going to have to get my handyman to come over, take the the dishwasher out and fix it so it is even on both sides. Oh - and both installers thought they had to go by the warehouse and pick up the dishwasher - were not informed it was already delivered. I thought I was getting a good deal because installation was included, but it was not worth the headaches. Need a new stove to match the fridge and dishwasher but I will go somewhere else. Never buying another appliance from Costco.

Sentence (English): This dishwasher automatically washes the dishes and does a nice job, however, drying the dishes must be done manually.
Comments (English): [ Greatly Disappointed ] || ---------------- || This dishwasher automatically washes the dishes and does a nice job, however, drying the dishes must be done manually. The manufacturer, using the excuse of optimizing energy efficiency, has devised a steam dry system that doesn't dry the dishes. I had the Bosch service person at may house who explained that with the 2022 top of the line models the following protocols are to be followed to dry the dishes: "Upon completion of the cycle, the dishes can be hand dried, or, if it works in one's schedule, the door can be manually propped open within one hour of cycle completion to allow the steam to escape." In this case, some of the dishes dry. The remaining dishes need hand drying. I have owned several Bosch dishwashers over the past 26 years and have always been a satisfied customer. No longer. I am stunned that Bosch would market this dishwasher and am in discussions with the Bosch dealer to resolve the situation.

Sentence (English): We bought Jan 5/23 to replace exactly (we thought) the same model we bought appropriately 5 years ago.
Comments (English): [ The Same but Not ] || ---------------- || We bought Jan 5/23 to replace exactly (we thought) the same model we bought appropriately 5 years ago. We liked this dishwasher because it looks good in our kitchen, cleaned the dishes well and was relatively quiet to run. However, it is not the same dishwasher. The material for the racks and the cutlery baskets is much thinner and lighter making us wonder if it will be at all durable. In our experience the racks with our daily usage begin to wear through after 4 or 5 years. The coating on the racks cracks and the metal underneath begins to rust. We do not wash pots or pans in the dishwasher and we make an effort to load the dishwasher gently. The other major change is the design of the cutlery baskets. Our previous baskets were sturdier and were clipped together so the entire solid unit could be brought to the counter making for quick unloading. These two baskets are independent and rather flimsy. The design is off as the rear basket cannot be clipped in properly using both rear clips. The top clip can work but then the basket sits on an angle leaving the bottom clip unable to catch. If the bottom rear clip is used on the rear basket then the top rear clip cannot engage. Conversely, if the rear basket is clipped in properly, the front basket cannot be. Our biggest disappointment is the depth of the cutlery basket. The depth of the basket is smaller. It doesn't support the knives, forks or tablespoons as upright. We have cutlery that is wider at the bottom end and we took the cutlery divider off one basket, causing the cutlery to flop over. This was not a problem in our previous dishwasher's baskets. The other change is instead of a Rinse and Hold cycle it is a Half Load cycle. My mother-in-law used her Rinse and Hold cycle every other day and washed the dishes for her and her husband the next day. This wasn't a cycle we used often but were more likely to use than a Half Load cycle. We bought this new dishwasher without seeing it first as we thought it would be the same as our old one. Time will tell if we buy it a third time.

Our previous baskets were sturdier and were clipped together so the entire solid unit could be brought to the counter making for quick unloading. These two baskets are independent and rather flimsy.  The design is off as the rear basket cannot be clipped in properly using both rear clips. The top clip can work but then the basket sits on an angle leaving the bottom clip unable to catch. If the bottom rear clip is used on the rear basket then the top rear clip cannot engage. Conversely, if the rear basket is clipped in properly, the front basket cannot be. Our biggest disappointment is the depth of the cutlery basket.  The depth of the basket is smaller.  It doesn't support the knives, forks or tablespoons as upright. We have cutlery that is wider at the bottom end and we took the cutlery divider off one basket, causing the cutlery to flop over.  This was not a problem in our previous dishwasher's baskets. The other change is instead of a Rinse and Hold cycle it is a Half Load cycle. My mother-in-law used her Rinse and Hold cycle every other day and washed the dishes for her and her husband the next day. This wasn't a cycle we used often but were more likely to use than a Half Load cycle.  We bought this new dishwasher without seeing it first as we thought it would be the same as our old one. Time will tell if we buy it a third time.
